build me catan. DO NOT ASK ANY QUESTIONS JUST COMPLETE

Implement EXACTLY this specification, do not redesign:

=== spec.md ===
Title: Settlers (Catan-style Hex Board Game, Server-Authoritative)
Genre: Turn-Based Strategy / Resource Management Board Game
Platform: Roblox (Luau), single CAS build; 3D hex board + ScreenGui HUD, mobile-friendly

## 1. Global Settings & Architecture
- Players: up to 4 seats (hot-seat on one client, or multiplayer). Minimum viable: 2-4 players cycling turns on one device.
- Authority: Server owns the board, dice, all resource/structure state, turn order, robber, and rule validation (prevents illegal placements/rolls). Client renders the board + HUD and forwards intents.
- Networking: `RemoteEvent` `RollDice`; `RemoteEvent` `PlaceStructure` (args `kind` "settlement"|"city"|"road", `nodeOrEdgeId`); `RemoteEvent` `MoveRobber` (args `tileId`, optional `victimSeat`); `RemoteEvent` `EndTurn`; `RemoteEvent` `StateSync` (server -> client: board, players' resources, structures, turn, phase, lastRoll, robberTile).
- Camera: `Scriptable`, angled top-down over the board, static.

## 2. Board Model (Hex Grid)
- Standard 19-tile hex island (radii 1-2-3-2-1 rows: 3,4,5,4,3 tiles).
- Tile fields: `tileId` 1..19, `resource` ("wood"|"brick"|"sheep"|"wheat"|"ore"|"desert"), `numberToken` (2..12 excluding 7; desert has none), `hasRobber` (bool).
- Resource distribution: 4 wood, 3 brick, 4 sheep, 4 wheat, 3 ore, 1 desert (18 producing + desert). Number tokens: standard set 2,3,3,4,4,5,5,6,6,8,8,9,9,10,10,11,11,12 assigned to non-desert tiles.
- Tile colors: wood/forest #2E7D32, brick #C0562B, sheep #9CCC65, wheat #F4C430, ore #78909C, desert #D8C79A.
- Graph: 54 vertices (settlement/city nodes) and 72 edges (road slots) derived from the hex layout; each vertex stores adjacent tiles (for resource yield) and adjacent vertices (for distance rule); each edge stores its two endpoint vertices.

## 3. Turn Structure & Phases
- Setup phase: snake-order initial placement - each player places 2 settlements + 2 roads (2nd settlement grants starting resources from adjacent tiles). Enforced before main play.
- Main turn sequence per active player:
 1. `roll` - must `RollDice` first (2d6).
 2. `produce/robber` - resolve the roll (Section 5).
 3. `build` - optionally place roads/settlements/cities and/or trade.
 4. `EndTurn` - advance to next seat.
- `currentSeat` cycles 1→2→...→N→1. Only the active seat may act; the server rejects actions from other seats or out-of-phase actions.

## 4. Dice Roll
- `RollDice`: server generates two independent d6 (1..6 each), sum 2..12, sets `lastRoll`, animates dice, and applies the outcome (Section 5). Only allowed in `roll` phase for the active player; produces a visible value reflected in state within 5s.

## 5. Resource Production & Robber
- Non-7 roll: every tile whose `numberToken == roll` and does NOT have the robber produces its resource for each settlement (×1) or city (×2) on its adjacent vertices; resources added to the owning players. This can award resources to multiple players in one roll.
- Roll of 7 (robber): NO normal production. Instead:
 1. Every player with > 7 resource cards discards half (rounded down).
 2. The active player must `MoveRobber` to a different tile; that tile is blocked (produces nothing while robbed).
 3. The active player steals 1 random resource from a player with a structure adjacent to the new robber tile (if any).
- Robber state (`robberTile`) is authoritative and visualized by a robber pawn on the tile.

## 6. Building Costs & Rules
- Costs: Road = 1 wood + 1 brick; Settlement = 1 wood + 1 brick + 1 sheep + 1 wheat; City = 2 wheat + 3 ore (upgrades an existing settlement).
- On `PlaceStructure`, server validates and rejects if any fail:
 - Sufficient resources for the cost (else reject: insufficient resources).
 - Settlement: target vertex empty AND satisfies the distance rule (no settlement/city on any directly adjacent vertex) AND (after setup) connected to the player's own road.
 - Road: target edge empty AND connected to the player's own existing road/settlement/city.
 - City: target vertex currently holds the player's own settlement (upgrades it).
- On success: deduct cost, register the structure to the seat, broadcast StateSync. Points: settlement = 1 VP, city = 2 VP. First to 10 VP wins.

## 7. User Interface (UI) & HUD - ScreenGui layout
Root: `ScreenGui` (IgnoreGuiInset=true).
- Top Center (Turn): "TurnLabel" "Player 2's Turn" in that player's color, TextSize 30 `GothamBold`, anchor (0.5,0)+(0,12).
- Top Left (Last Roll): "RollLabel" showing two dice faces + sum, TextSize 28.
- Bottom (Resource Bar `ResourceBar`): full-width, height 96px, #1E1230 85%; 5 resource counters (Wood/Brick/Sheep/Wheat/Ore) with icon + count via `UIListLayout`, for the ACTIVE player. Counts update live.
- Bottom Right (Action buttons): "RollButton" (visible in roll phase), "BuildSettlement"/"BuildRoad"/"BuildCity" toggle buttons (build phase), "EndTurnButton". Laid out in a `UIListLayout`; if crowded, a `ScrollingFrame` keeps every action reachable.
- Build mode: selecting "BuildSettlement/Road/City" highlights all LEGAL vertices/edges (translucent #FFD93D markers); tapping a marker confirms placement.
- Victory Point tracker: small per-player VP chips top-right.
- Game Over overlay: "Player N Wins!" + Restart.
- Layout safety: turn/roll in top 72px, resource bar + actions in bottom ~150px, board in the middle; scroll ensures no counter/action clipped or off-screen.

## 8. Input & Screen-to-Board Mapping
- Placement uses discrete legal-target markers: in build mode the server sends the set of legal vertex/edge ids; the client shows a marker at each. A tap raycasts (`Camera:ScreenPointToRay`) and selects the nearest legal marker within 3 studs of the hit → `PlaceStructure(kind, id)`. Because each vertex/edge has a distinct marker and the ray uses the exact tapped pixel, the structure is placed at the tapped board location (intended vertex/edge), not a neighbor.
- Dice: tapping RollButton (a discrete `TextButton`) fires `RollDice`.
- Server re-validates every placement (Section 6) regardless of client markers, so illegal taps are rejected.

## 9. Audio
- `dice_roll.mp3` (0.5); `build.mp3` (0.5) on placement; `resource_gain.mp3` (0.4) on production; `robber.mp3` (0.5) on a 7; `steal.mp3` (0.4); `turn_change.mp3` (0.3); `victory.mp3` (0.6). Client-side.

## 10. Visual Style & Polish
- Palette: tiles per Section 2; player colors P1 #E74C3C, P2 #3498DB, P3 #F1C40F, P4 #2ECC71; legal-target markers #FFD93D; robber pawn #2C2C2C.
- Dice: 3D tumble animation settling on the rolled faces (0.6s).
- Settlement/city meshes in player color; roads as colored bars along edges.
- Number tokens: circular tiles with the number; 6 and 8 rendered in red (high-probability), others black.
- Resource gain: floating "+1 wood" text over producing vertices.

## 11. Roblox Feasibility Notes
- `ServerScriptService/CatanServer` holds the board graph (precomputed 19 tiles / 54 vertices / 72 edges adjacency), rules, and turn state; `StarterPlayerScripts/CatanClient` renders the board and HUD and does ScreenPointToRay placement. Turn-based → StateSync only on changes. Board graph is precomputed data (no runtime geometry solving). Scope (single island, core rules, no trading UI beyond bank optional) is realistic for one CAS build. Discrete markers make placement mobile-friendly.

## 12. Acceptance Criteria (maps 1:1 to test_plan core + advanced items)
- **AC-play_starts (core):** On Play, within 10s a hex board with resource tiles + number tokens AND a player/resource HUD are visible with no startup errors. (Sections 2, 7.)
- **AC-roll_dice (core):** A dice roll (2d6) produces a visible value and updates game state within 5s (only in roll phase for the active player). (Sections 3, 4.)
- **AC-place_settlement_road (core):** A settlement and/or road is placed at a valid vertex/edge and registered in state; invalid placements are rejected. (Sections 6, 8.)
- **AC-resources_and_turns (advanced):** After a roll, resources are awarded to players by adjacent structures on matching tiles, and EndTurn advances currentSeat to a different player. (Sections 3, 5.)
- **AC-robber_on_seven (advanced):** Rolling a 7 triggers the robber (no normal production; over-limit discards; robber moves/blocks a tile; steal) rather than distributing resources. (Section 5.)
- **AC-building_costs_and_rules (advanced):** Building deducts the correct cost AND illegal placements (insufficient resources or violating adjacency/distance/connectivity) are rejected. (Section 6.)
- **AC-input_mapping (advanced):** Discrete legal-target markers + exact-pixel raycast mean a settlement/road is placed at the tapped vertex/edge, not a neighbor. (Section 8.)
- **AC-no_runtime_errors (core):** Server validates seat/phase/cost/adjacency and uses a precomputed bounds-safe graph; no red console output. (Sections 3, 6, 11.)
- **AC-ui_layout_quality (polish):** Turn/roll (top 72px), resource bar + actions (bottom ~150px) never overlap and stay on-screen; scroll prevents clipping. (Section 7.)
- **AC-gameplay_clarity (polish):** Whose turn it is, the active player's resources, and available actions (roll/build/end) are clear from the HUD with no wall-of-text. (Section 7.)


=== plan.md ===
# Settlers (Catan-style)

A server-authoritative hex board game: roll 2d6 to produce resources, build roads/settlements/cities under cost and adjacency rules, handle the robber on a 7, and cycle turns toward 10 victory points.

## Milestones
1. **Board & Networking** - Precomputed 19-tile hex board with 54 vertices / 72 edges, resource/token distribution, and RemoteEvents (RollDice, PlaceStructure, MoveRobber, EndTurn, StateSync). Maps to spec §1, §2.
2. **Turn Structure & Dice** - Setup snake placement, roll/produce/build/end phases, active-seat enforcement, 2d6 roll. Maps to spec §3, §4.
3. **Production & Robber** - Resource yield by number token and adjacent structures, 7-roll robber (discard/move/steal). Maps to spec §5.
4. **Building Rules** - Costs and validation for roads/settlements/cities (resources, distance, connectivity, upgrade), VP tracking and win at 10. Maps to spec §6.
5. **HUD & Placement Input** - Turn/roll HUD, active-player resource bar, action buttons, legal-target markers, raycast placement mapping. Maps to spec §7, §8.
6. **Audio & Polish** - Dice/build/resource/robber/turn/victory SFX, 3D dice tumble, colored structures, number-token styling, layout QA and acceptance pass. Maps to spec §9, §10, §12.

answers.ask: How big should the physical board be in studs - a table-sized board or a walkable arena-sized one?
answers.answer: Use a table-sized board; this is a static, top-down board game and does not need a walkable arena.

scene_prompt: Create a static, table-sized 3D hex-board game map viewed by a fixed angled top-down camera. Arrange a standard 19-tile hexagonal island in five staggered rows of 3, 4, 5, 4, and 3 terrain hexes, with forest, brick-clay, pasture, wheat field, ore, and one central or near-central desert tile; each producing hex has a circular numbered token, with 6 and 8 tokens red. Place a dark robber pawn on the desert at the start. Surround the board edges with 54 settlement/city vertex positions and 72 road slots, visibly integrated along tile corners and borders. Show player-colored settlements, cities, and road bars when built, plus a pair of 3D dice beside the board. Keep the board unobstructed in the middle of the screen, with space around it for a top turn-and-roll HUD and bottom resource/action controls.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy because this is explicitly a turn-based resource-management board game controlled from a fixed camera.

## Shape and preset
Use `board-grid` for a table-sized hex board that users act on rather than traverse. Match the Board & Card Games preset, adapting its regular playing spaces to the specified hex graph.

## Config requirements
Apply `tile-grid` as exactly 19 terrain hexes in staggered rows of 3, 4, 5, 4, and 3. Draw 4 forest, 3 brick-clay, 4 pasture, 4 wheat, 3 ore, and 1 central or near-central desert. Give all 18 producing tiles circular number tokens; color 6 and 8 red and all others black. Include one dark robber pawn, player-color wooden settlements, cities, and road bars, and exactly two 3D dice beside the island.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly 54 unique settlement/city vertex sockets at hex corners and exactly 72 unique road slots along valid borders, deduplicating shared geometry and preserving the precomputed adjacency graph. Place the robber on the single desert tile initially. Associate each number token with its producing hex. Reserve structure sockets for dynamic player-colored builds; do not prefill them as permanent scenery.

## Layout components
Build one table-sized island board centered in the camera-safe middle area. Its 19 equal hexes form the exact five-row silhouette with perfectly aligned shared edges. Place the desert centrally or near-centrally and distribute the five producing terrain families in a readable mix. Number tokens sit at tile centers without hiding terrain identity. Vertex sockets and edge slots remain visually integrated but selectable. Put the two dice just outside the island footprint on the tabletop. Leave generous neutral margin above for turn and roll information and below for resources and actions. Compose the plan symmetrically and keep every tile, token, edge, and corner unobstructed.

## Render order
Render `topdown` first and treat it as authoritative, then dress the isometric view from that plan, because the exact 19-tile arrangement and 54-vertex/72-edge graph must be spatially valid.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale is small and table-sized. The theme is polished colorful resource-board terrain with wooden pieces. Use `P0` with `SET`: nobody walks on the geometry, so traversal and jump-gap checks are skipped.
